chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abū al-Jawzā', from al-Ḥusayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn 'Alī, from his forefathers, from 'Alī عليه السلام, who said:

A group came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said, “A woman died while with us, and there was no mahram with her.” He said, “What did you do?” They said, “We poured water over her.” He said, “Could you not find a woman from among the People of the Book to perform ghusl for her?” They said, “No.” He said, “Then why did you not perform tayammum for her?”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book, here referring to a non-Muslim scriptural community member
key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهَا: to wash her body ritually after death
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a person within the unmarriageable kin whose presence affects legal rulings of bodily handling
key_terms.يَمَّمْتُمُوهَا: you performed tayammum for her as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: What should be done for the body of a deceased woman if no mahram or female washer is available?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the handling of a deceased woman when no mahram is present to wash her. It indicates that if a Muslim woman is unavailable, a woman from the People of the Book may perform the ghusl, and if that is not possible, tayammum should be performed instead. The report is significant in jurisprudence for rulings related to ritual purity and funeral preparation.
